title: Returns
outcomes: Apply GSTR-1, IFF and GSTR-1A provisions.
Apply annual, final and special returns.
Compute late fees and apply time-bar.

meta.exam_tip: Write due dates as day plus month-after-period to avoid confusion.

concepts.title: Outward supply statements — GSTR-1 and IFF
body: Section 37: details of outward supplies are furnished in GSTR-1 by the 11th of the next month (monthly filers) or 13th of the month after the quarter (QRMP). Optional Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) lets QRMP taxpayers upload B2B invoices for the first two months by the 13th of the following month.

GSTR-1A allows amendments or missed details for the same tax period before filing GSTR-3B. GSTR-1 cannot be filed if GSTR-3B for the previous period is pending, and filing of GSTR-1 is a precondition for GSTR-3B of the same period.
HSN details in GSTR-1 depend on turnover (4 digits up to ₹5 crore for B2B; 6 digits above). Errors can be corrected up to 30 November after the year or the annual return date, whichever earlier.
concepts.analogy: GSTR-1 tells buyers what you sold; it feeds their ITC.
concepts.work: A monthly filer submits June GSTR-1 by 11 July.

concepts.title: GSTR-3B and the QRMP scheme
body: Section 39: GSTR-3B is the summary return with self-assessed tax and payment, due by the 20th of the next month for monthly filers; QRMP filers (turnover up to ₹5 crore) file quarterly by the 22nd or 24th depending on State, paying tax monthly via PMT-06 by the 25th using fixed-sum or self-assessment methods.
A return is valid only if self-assessed tax is paid in full. Returns must be signed with DSC (mandatory for companies and LLPs), e-sign or EVC.
The Invoice Management System lets recipients accept, reject or keep pending invoices before GSTR-2B is generated, affecting ITC.
concepts.analogy: GSTR-3B is where tax is actually paid.
concepts.work: A Maharashtra QRMP filer files quarterly GSTR-3B by the 22nd.

concepts.title: Annual return, final return and other returns
body: Section 44: annual return GSTR-9 by 31 December after the year; optional for taxpayers with turnover up to ₹2 crore; self-certified reconciliation statement GSTR-9C for turnover above ₹5 crore. Composition taxpayers file GSTR-4 annually by 30 April and pay quarterly via CMP-08 by the 18th.
Section 45: a final return GSTR-10 within three months of cancellation or the date of cancellation order, whichever later.

Other returns: GSTR-5 (non-resident taxable persons), GSTR-5A (OIDAR suppliers), GSTR-6 (ISD), GSTR-7 (TDS), GSTR-8 (TCS). Section 46 notices are issued to non-filers, and best judgement assessment can follow.
concepts.analogy: Annual, final and special returns complete the cycle.
concepts.work: A firm with ₹12 crore turnover files both GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C.

concepts.title: Late fee and time-bar
body: Section 47: late fee for GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B is reduced by notification to ₹50 per day (₹20 per day for nil returns) with caps of ₹2,000 (turnover up to ₹1.5 crore), ₹5,000 (₹1.5–5 crore) and ₹10,000 (above ₹5 crore) — amounts total CGST and SGST.

GSTR-9 late fee: ₹50 per day up to ₹5 crore turnover and ₹100 per day for ₹5–20 crore, capped at 0.04% of State turnover; higher for larger taxpayers. GSTR-4: ₹50 per day capped at ₹2,000 (₹20 per day and ₹500 cap if nil). GSTR-7: ₹50 per day capped at ₹1,000.
Returns (GSTR-1, 3B, 4, 5, 5A, 6, 7, 8, 9) cannot be filed after three years from their due dates. Late fee may be waived in part or full by notification (section 128).
concepts.analogy: Late fees are per day with caps; returns time-bar after three years.
concepts.work: A ₹3 crore trader filing GSTR-3B 120 days late pays a capped ₹5,000.

jobs.title: Return calendar
jobs.situation: A client with several registrations keeps missing due dates.
steps: Map monthly and quarterly due dates.
Use IMS to manage supplier invoices.
Pay via PMT-06 for QRMP months.
jobs.takeaway: A calendar avoids fees and blocked ITC for customers.
